original_test_intent: Invoke TelemetryService.SubmitTestMetricReport to generate one test report, while the preserved Procedure only performs GET on the action URI.
original_method: After resolving the method conflict, validate one approved definition and baseline report inventory, obtain confirmation, POST the exact documented action once, follow any bounded task, verify the attributable report and execute only the approved retention/cleanup policy.
manual_activity: Resolve GET versus POST, select an approved MetricReportDefinition, approve the expected report side effect and decide whether the generated artifact must be retained or removed by a supported method.
required_inputs: Firmware action URI and payload schema
safety_requirements: Never treat GET on an action URI as action coverage
No hardcoded secrets or unapproved TLS bypass
Use only an existing approved definition
No blind retry after timeout or ambiguous response
Correlate the report to this action
Do not promise cleanup unless the vendor supports and approves it
agent_execution_scope: Validate the selected definition and expected metrics
Poll task and report inventory within bounds
Validate its definition reference and metric content
engineer_actions: Approve side effect, retention and cleanup
Own ambiguous-artifact handling and final DUT verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: POST matches the Items but materially replaces the Master GET. The payload name is operator-controlled, collection verification is ID-only, and no task/correlation/retention contract prevents duplicate or persistent artifacts.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: With approved schema and definition, capture baseline, submit exactly once over verified TLS, follow the returned task/location, correlate one new report by schema-defined identity and execute the preapproved artifact policy.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The named action and 15/10 timing remain; no definition name, payload property, task duration, report lifetime or delete support is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat report submission as a single state-changing transaction with before/after inventory, response/task correlation and explicit artifact ownership.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Corrects GET to POST only under approval and adds payload schema, definition validation, one-shot ambiguity handling, attributable report checks and retention/cleanup governance.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Covers one manual test-report submission for one existing definition; it does not validate scheduled generation, create definitions, exercise all metrics or stress storage limits.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A timeout may still have created a report, and some implementations retain generated reports without a delete action; retries or guessed cleanup can multiply or remove unrelated artifacts.

project_override_considerations: Use the action target and parameter names advertised by the target schema, not the DeepSeek payload by assumption. If reports are overwritten rather than appended, compare timestamps/content and preserve the prior artifact according to policy.
expected_evidence: Approved definition and expected metric set
Single POST status and response/task location
One correlated report identity and content
Unchanged unrelated definitions/reports and preserved logs

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and Script require a POST action, but the Master Procedure issues GET to the action URI. GET cannot submit or validate a report, so the method conflict is material and must not be silently repaired.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The action schema, approved definition, confirmation and artifact policy are concrete prerequisites, making the case REQUIRES rather than permanently BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Stops an inert GET from passing a state-changing POST case and constrains the real action to one approved definition with unambiguous correlation and governed residual telemetry data.
independent_technical_reasoning: SubmitTestMetricReport is not merely a read of an action endpoint: it can create or replace telemetry data and may return asynchronously. If the POST times out, absence of a client response does not prove absence of a report, so a retry can create a duplicate; resolution must begin with task/location and inventory reads. Report identity must be tied to the selected definition and action time, not just be any new member ID. Because Redfish implementations may not expose deletion for generated reports, retention is an execution decision, not a cleanup assumption.
